name: Wüste Fraktale
classification_notes: A classic fraktur letter skeleton rebuilt entirely from handcrafted pixel blocks, putting a digital, low-resolution texture on a traditional blackletter form.
summary: A classic fraktur blackletter rebuilt out of 243 handcrafted pixelated letters.
description: Wüste Fraktale keeps the broken, angular skeleton of a traditional fraktur but renders every letter in blocky, pixelated units, landing somewhere between medieval blackletter and early screen type. It works best at the display sizes its texture is built for.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts describe Wüste Fraktale as a classic blackletter fraktur typeface made up of 243 handcrafted pixelated letters.

name: Ghana Signpainters Divine Healer
classification_notes: Uppercase-only display letters copied from hand-painted signage, with the irregular stroke widths and confident shapes of brush lettering rather than a drafted alphabet.
summary: An uppercase-only display face copied from hand-painted shop signage seen in Ghana.
description: Divine Healer is one of three Ghana Signpainters faces built directly from hand-painted signs, capitals only, with the confident, slightly uneven strokes of brush lettering rather than a drawn alphabet. It sits alongside sibling cuts Safari and Cocktail in the same series.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts say Divine Healer is one of three fonts inspired by handpainted signs in Ghana, and that it doesn't contain lowercase letters.

name: Ghana Signpainters Safari
classification_notes: Another uppercase-only cut in the same hand-painted signage series as Divine Healer, sharing its vernacular brush-lettering roots but with its own set of letterforms.
summary: A second uppercase-only face in the Ghana Signpainters series, drawn from hand-painted shop signage.
description: Safari shares its source material with Divine Healer: hand-painted signs photographed in Ghana, redrawn as capitals-only display letters. Its own particular stroke shapes give it a separate character within the same series.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts say Safari is one of three fonts inspired by handpainted signs in Ghana, and that it doesn't contain lowercase letters.

name: Internationale
classification_notes: A plain, functional display alphabet pitched at packaging and stencil-style labelling rather than editorial or branding text.
summary: A plain, deadpan display face the foundry pitches at labelling crates rather than any grander use.
description: Internationale is a small, functional display alphabet with no pretensions beyond doing a practical labelling job well, in keeping with Kiosk Fonts' habit of building type around a specific, slightly absurd brief.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts say Internationale should be used to label tea-filled crates.

name: Black Frituur
classification_notes: Fuses the broken, angular structure of blackletter with the round, connected shapes of written script, landing between the two rather than settling as a strict fraktur.
summary: A blackletter and script hybrid that softens fraktur's broken edges with round, connected script shapes.
description: Black Frituur sits between two traditions at once, taking the broken and edgy shapes of blackletter and rounding them off with the softer curves of written script, for a display face with more warmth than a straight fraktur.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts describe Black Frituur as combining the broken and edgy shapes of a blackletter font with the round and soft shapes of written script.

name: Druckerei
classification_notes: A display face built around contextual OpenType substitution, cycling through up to five variants per glyph to mimic the irregularity of hand printing rather than presenting a fixed alphabet.
summary: A display face that swaps in one of up to five variants per glyph via OpenType, for a quasi-random, hand-printed texture.
description: Druckerei uses a contextual OpenType feature to replace typed letters with one of up to five alternate glyph variants in quasi-random fashion, so no two words look quite the same and the whole thing reads like it came off an inked press rather than a screen.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts say Druckerei sports up to five different variants per glyph, with a specially developed contextsensitive OpenType feature replacing typed letters with variants to achieve an almost handprinted appearance.

name: Roundenau Basic
classification_notes: The free basic character set of a rounded sans family, with a fuller Advanced set planned as a paid companion.
summary: A free rounded sans covering the basic character set, with a fuller Advanced version planned as a paid release.
description: Roundenau Basic gives away the essential character set of Kiosk Fonts' rounded sans project at no cost, with a more complete Roundenau Advanced set intended as a future paid companion.
foundry_blurb: Kiosk Fonts describe Roundenau Basic as free and containing the basic typeset, with Roundenau Advanced planned to contain the advanced typeset.
